Career Category Sales & Marketing OperationsJob Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Contracts & Pricing Strategy, Associate Director What you will do The Contracts & Pricing Strategy Associate Director leads integrated U.S. pricing and contracting economics for OaR across launch and lifecycle planning. Reporting to the Dir Contracts & Pricing Strategy, the role translates the overall Obesity and Related Conditions contracts, pricing and value strategy into payer and Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBM) recommendations, Gross to Net (GTN) and latest estimate discount rate (LEDR) process, and coordinated channel economics. The role partners with the Consumer Director and Employer Lead Director to incorporate approved assumptions while they retain channel strategy and relationships. Prior-authorization and utilization-management analysis remain with the Coverage Lead. Core responsibilities: Pricing and contracting strategy: - Lead development of U.S. pricing and contracting recommendations for MariTide across commercial, Medicare and Medicaid channels across all payers and pharmacy benefit managers (PBM) - Build account and portfolio economics, bid and negotiation scenarios, access-price trade-offs and guardrails. - Partner with Coverage, Market Access, Contract Development and Contracting and Pricing Execution to translate approved strategy into executable contract terms. Integrated GTN and business planning: - Lead the Obesity latest estimate discount rate (LEDR) process and maintain the integrated gross to net (GTN) and net-sales view used in launch planning, quarterly business reviews and long-range planning. - Reconcile rebates, fees, affordability, trade, government and channel-mix assumptions; run base, upside and downside scenarios; document key dependencies; and explain actual-to-plan variances and changes in forward assumptions. Consumer and employer economics: - Partner with the Consumer Director and Employer Lead Director to incorporate approved retail-pharmacy, cash-reimbursement and Direct to Employer (DTE) assumptions into gross to net (GTN). - Model patient contribution, pharmacy and fulfillment fees, employer and member contributions, program fees, eligible lives, sites, enrollment, activation, utilization, persistence and ramp. - Govern membership inputs and reconcile patient migration and population overlap across channels. Launch and lifecycle pricing: - Translate Global value and pricing considerations into U.S. launch scenarios and communicate U.S. channel implications to Global partners. - Develop assumptions, analogs, sensitivity ranges and decision triggers where actuals do not exist. - Extend the pricing and gross to net (GTN) architecture to future indications and sequencing decisions as populations, evidence, benefit management, utilization and channel mix evolve. Governance and cross-functional leadership: - Lead cross-functional pricing workstreams with Finance, Forecasting, Accounting, Government Pricing, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Trade, Brand and Market Access. - Establish common model definitions, documentation and review cadence; identify duplicate-discount, classification, reporting, privacy and channel-conflict risks; and present clear recommendations, alternatives and unresolved issues to the Director and senior governance. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is someone with these qualifications. Basic qualifications: - Doctorate degree and 3 years of pricing, contracting, market access, finance, accounting, analytics or sales and marketing operations experience; OR - Master’s degree and 5 years of pricing, contracting, market access, finance, accounting, analytics or sales and marketing operations experience; OR - Bachelor’s degree and 7 years of pricing, contracting, market access, finance, accounting, analytics or sales and marketing operations experience; OR - Associate’s degree and 12 years of pricing, contracting, market access, finance, accounting, analytics or sales and marketing operations experience; OR - High school diploma or GED and 14 years of pricing, contracting, market access, finance, accounting, analytics or sales and marketing operations experience. Preferred qualifications: - Substantial U.S. pharmaceutical pricing, payer or PBM contracting, GTN forecasting or launch financial-planning experience, ideally in a high-volume chronic or cardiometabolic market. - Demonstrated ownership of an enterprise forecast or economic model that integrates assumptions from multiple business owners and supports senior decisions. - Experience with reimbursed, cash, employer, affordability, trade and government flows and their implications for GTN and price reporting. - Ability to govern eligible-life and membership cohorts, channel migration, transaction economics, data lineage and model controls. - Strong executive communication and influence without direct authority; advanced Excel and enterprise planning or deal-modeling experience preferred. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include: - A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts - A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan - Stock-based long-term incentives - Award-winning time-off plans - Flexible work models where possible. data.description:
Senior Director, AP Assessment Design and Insights College Board – AP&I Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes. Role Type: This is a full-time position About the Team The College Board’s Advanced Placement and Instruction division (300+ staff) develops and administers coursework taken by more than 3 million students worldwide each school year, and the related subject-matter exams utilized by more than 4,000 colleges and universities for course placement and awarding of college credit. These include credit and placement examination programs like CLEP and ACCUplacer; Advanced Placement (AP) and Pre-AP courses in 40+ disciplines; and associated teacher professional learning programs. To support the continued growth and evolution of the program, the AP Program Enablement team is designed to oversee the end-to-end management of the AP Course Roadmap, as well as the assessment design and systems requirements, processes and production functions that underpin all new and existing AP courses and exams. This team plays a central role in ensuring alignment, quality, and efficiency across the full lifecycle of course and assessment production. Within AP Program Enablement, the AP Assessment Design & Systems team functions as the cross-cutting backbone accountable for the assessment design, systems, and requirements making “build to score and report” possible across all AP courses and exams. Assessment Design & Systems governs the end-to-end integration across the full platform ecosystem, assessment design and requirements, the integrity and certification layer, and the knowledge and data governance, serving as the connective tissue other Program Enablement functions rely on to operate as one coherent system. This scope spans all 40+ existing AP courses and new courses in active development and underpins the program’s digital transformation and strategic priorities. About the Opportunity As Senior Director, AP Assessment Design and Insights, you will serve as a senior strategic leader and analytical engine within the AP Assessment Design & Systems team within AP Program Enablement, driving the assessment design infrastructure, systems strategy, and knowledge architecture that underpin AP’s assessment work across existing courses and a growing portfolio of new course development. This role sits at the intersection of assessment design, data-informed strategy, and cross-functional leadership, and is essential to ensuring that AP’s assessment design, systems, and resources are coherent, current, and positioned for the program’s long-term evolution. You will lead and advance AP's assessment design infrastructure, from intake frameworks for new and revised courses to the team's assessment resources, knowledge base, and systems roadmap, working in close partnership with the Executive Director, who sets the strategic direction for the team. You will serve as an authoritative voice on assessment design standards and requirements across the AP ecosystem, a trusted partner to technology and product teams, and the primary driver of the divisional AP Assessment Community of Practice. This is an ideal role for a senior assessment leader who combines deep expertise in educational assessment with the strategic and analytical capabilities to advance a complex, high-stakes program at scale.
